facts.label: Past progressive e passado simples
facts.sub: Conte histórias: I was sitting when the lights went out. Use was/were + -ing para a ação longa e passado simples para a curta.

facts.label: Ação em andamento
facts.sub: Para uma ação em andamento no passado, use was/were + -ing: I was eating a sandwich. Everyone was laughing. Use was com I, he, she e it, e were com you, we e they.

facts.label: Ação curta
facts.sub: Para uma ação curta que interrompe, use o passado simples: A bird stole it. The lights went out. Os verbos stole e went são irregulares.

compare.ask: I was eating when a bird stole it.
compare.br: No Brasil, dizemos “Eu estava comendo quando o pássaro roubou”.
compare.tip: Diga: “I was eating when a bird stole it.”
compare.us: Em inglês: was/were + -ing para a ação longa e passado simples para a curta, com when. Diga I was eating when a bird stole it.

solo: Peça uma experiência pessoal do aluno com essa diferença.
group: Leia as duas colunas e peça que apontem a maior diferença.

extra90: Dupla: um fala como no Brasil, o outro como nos EUA.

paragraphs: It is Friday afternoon at a bus stop in Glasgow. Children walk home with bags. Dan waits for the bus with a paper map. His friend Tina arrives with an umbrella. She sees his happy face. She asks about the trip.
“Hi, Dan! How was the school trip?” says Tina. “It was great! We visited the science museum.” says Dan. “What did you do there?” says Tina.
